title: feat(motion): the converter from a kernel plan to a toolpath
body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

## What changed

This PR adds the converter from a kernel `Plan` to a `Toolpath` in `camcraft-motion` (`crates/motion/src/kernel_emit/`). No old planner and no app code calls it. With the default planner switch, the output does not change. The first recipe (#3752) calls it.

The converter emits the steps of each level in the plan's order. It makes no decision of its own. It refuses a step that it cannot emit, with a named reason. It never drops a step and it never adds a cut.

Public surface (`camcraft_motion::kernel_emit`):
- `emit_plan(&Plan, WorkPlane, EmitHeights, EmitFeeds) -> Result<Emitted, EmitRefusal>`
- `emit_levels(&[LevelPlan { plan, plane }], EmitHeights, EmitFeeds) -> Result<Emitted, EmitRefusal>` (the levels in the order that the caller gives)
- `EmitHeights::new(clearance_z, top_z)` and `EmitFeeds::new(cut, plunge)`: checked values
- `Emitted { path, cut_moves: Vec<Range<usize>>, entries, stays, lifts, exits }`
- `EmitRefusal { reason(), level(), step() }`, `Display` and `Error`
- The refusal constants: `BAD_HEIGHTS`, `BAD_FEEDS`, `NOT_SETUP_XY`, `AXIS_NOT_NORMAL`, `UNKNOWN_STEP`, `ENTRY_NOT_CLEAR`, `APPROACH_IN_MATERIAL`, `STEP_OFF_TOOL`, `STEP_NOT_DOWN`, `ENDS_DOWN`, `ARC_OFF_CIRCLE`, `ARC_NOT_MONOTONE`, `CUT_DROPPED`, `NOT_FINITE`

The move rules (the safety floor):
- A lateral rapid is only at or above the clearance height. A rapid along the tool axis goes only up: the retract of a lift or of an exit.
- The move down from the clearance height to the approach is a plunge-feed move.
- Below the stock top there are only the moves of a proved step: a cut, a stay-down link, the descent and lead of an entry, the lead-out of an exit.
- Each step must start where the tool stands. Else the converter refuses with `STEP_OFF_TOOL`.
- A lift is a retract to the clearance height. Its named reason goes to the notes in the text form of `links.rs` (`link: the tool lifted to the clearance height N time(s) instead of the keep-down in-plane link - <reason>; ...`).
- A cut whose curve holds an exact circle becomes G2/G3 arcs (quarter turns that end on plan points). Arc leads, helices and ramps are chords in the plan (#4178 point 5). The converter emits them as feeds.
- The converter refuses a plane that is not the setup XY plane (`NOT_SETUP_XY`). The mapping reads the `WorkPlane`: Z is the plane origin plus the depth.

No kernel source changes. No accessor was added to the kernel crate.

The merge of `side/path-kernel` (df9ec30, the load stage of #4265) gave a conflict in the K4 test helper. The resolution keeps both sides: the load stage goes between order and link in the plan builder, and the path goes through the real converter.

The merge-time refresh merges `side/path-kernel` (fd653b0, PR #4275: the approach from the air of #4254). Two files conflicted:
- `k3_load.rs`: the Outside rows of #4275 hold on the merged tree with the cuts-only path of this PR. The row 337 / 77 of this PR is replaced.
- `k4_order_link.rs`: the module text of both sides is kept. The pin keeps the real converter and takes the lift counts of #4275 (0 on each case).

The converter emits the approach stretches as feeds of a stay-down link. It refuses nothing.

## Pins

- `kernel_emit::tests` (motion lib, 7 tests):
  - `each_step_kind_gives_its_moves`
  - `a_lift_writes_its_reason_to_the_notes`
  - `an_exact_circle_becomes_arcs`
  - `levels_are_emitted_in_the_given_order`
  - `nothing_is_dropped` (the count of cuts in equals the count of cut move groups out)
  - `a_step_that_cannot_be_emitted_is_refused_by_name`
  - `an_empty_plan_gives_an_empty_path`
- `kernel_laws::k4_order_link::kernel_order_and_link_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone`: the test helper is replaced. The test now builds the whole plan (guide, order, link, entry and exit stage, with a helix asked) and converts it with the real converter. The helper asserts the converter's counts of cuts, entries, stay-down links, lifts and exits against the plan. On the merged tree:
  - 0 lifts on each case (#4275)
  - each lift named
  - the feed crossings as measured (`CROSSINGS`): disc Outside 3, dog bone Outside 1, Inside 0 (see the findings, follow-up #4300)
- `kernel_laws::k6a_plan_emit::the_verifier_finds_no_rapid_into_stock_and_no_plunge_without_an_entry` (new): the `camcraft-sim` verifier on the converted disc and dog-bone plans, Inside and Outside. It finds no `RapidInStock`, no `RapidInPart`, no `PlungeIntoStock` and no `Gouge`. Each descent below the stock top is a plan entry. Each descent into solid stock is a helix or a ramp.

## Readings and findings

| Fixture | Moves | Lifts (named) | Entries | Verifier |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| disc, Inside | 7336 | 0 | 1 into solid (read as a ramp: the helix is chords) | nothing |
| disc, Outside | 6497 | 0 | 1 in air | 3 `Crossing` |
| dog bone, Inside | 5368 | 0 | 1 into solid (ramp) | nothing |
| dog bone, Outside | 4719 | 0 | 1 in air | 1 `Crossing` |

These readings are on the merged tree (with #4275). Before #4275: 7355, 6402 (13 lifts, 14 entries), 5368, 4784 (15 lifts, 16 entries), and no verifier warning.

- **New with the merge: feed crossings in the air (Outside).** A stay-down link of #4275 runs along the air line (y -29) to the door of its approach. It crosses the arc lead of the first entry (moves 2 to 11). Disc: moves 189, 1664 and 1882 cross move 5 at (-38.398, -28.993). Dog bone: move 33 crosses move 5 at (4.587, -28.866). The link stage proves a link against the cuts, the links and the planned cuts, not against the leads of the entry stage. The kernel's test pen emits no leads, so #4275 read 0. The verifier finds no `RapidInStock`, no `RapidInPart`, no `PlungeIntoStock` and no `Gouge`: it reports the crossings as `Crossing` warnings only. The K4 pin asserts the counts as measured, so a new crossing makes it red. Follow-up: #4300 (the link proof reads the entry leads).
- The disc Inside path has 7336 moves, not 7355: the link tries of #4275 change some link routes. No count changes.

- First, the verifier area was the band of `fixture::band` (the stock grown by 2 tool radii, less the part). With that area, the verifier gave 72 and 84 `Gouge` warnings on Outside. Each one is on an air entry or its arc lead outside the band, 17 mm or more from the part. The pin now uses the stock grown by 4 tool radii, less the part. No warning is near the part.
- The law measure reads Outside feeds outside `fixture::centre_reach`: 44 (disc) and 52 (dog bone) before #4275, 4 and 3 on the merged tree (one air entry each). These are the arc leads in the air. This is a reading of the entry stage, not of the converter. No pin asserts it.
- **The side head df9ec30 was red in `k3_load`.** #4265 was gated on a branch without #4253 (the link edge band). On the side head df9ec30, the disc Outside row with constant engagement reads 337 moves above the limit and 77 unnamed, not 334 and 74. The old test pen gives the same 337. This PR pinned the row as measured. After the merge of #4275 the rows of #4275 hold (table below).
- `k3_load` measures the cuts of the load stage. It now reads `cuts_path_with`: the same plan, without the entry leads, with the moves of the old test pen. A temporary test compared the two paths: they have the same moves and the same notes.

## Gates (final head)

All on head `143a6ffafba794b4575b2c263ea919b2b92a0d02` (the merge-time refresh: the merge of `origin/side/path-kernel` fd653b0, with PR #4275):
- `cargo check --tests -p camcraft-motion`: pass
- `cargo check --tests -p camcraft-pathkernel`: pass
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib kernel_emit`: 7 passed
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test kernel_laws`: 31 passed (with `k3_load`, `k4_order_link`, `k6a_plan_emit`)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel --test laws`: 140 passed
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel`: 13 steps, 0 failed. The steps were motion lib, motion kernel_laws, and the app suites `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `catalog_groove_part_off`, `continuous_4axis_part`, `first_4axis_part`, `first_part_programs`, `first_router_part`, `tilt_basis_compat`.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: not run on this head (7 steps, 0 failed on `b2b596b`).

The `k3_load` rows on the merged tree (feed moves above the limit, the worst engagement, the unnamed moves; without load control / with constant engagement):

| Case | This PR on b2b596b | #4275 | Merged (143a6ff) |

| disc Inside | [3507, 173, 0] / [833, 173, 1] | same | same |
| disc Outside | [402, 145, 13] / [337, 118, 77] | [415, 145, 19] / [344, 122, 81] | [415, 145, 19] / [344, 122, 81] |
| dog bone Inside | [2587, 173, 0] / [581, 173, 1] | same | same |
| dog bone Outside | [724, 167, 3] / [678, 143, 66] | [739, 180, 13] / [683, 143, 69] | [739, 180, 13] / [683, 143, 69] |

Writer records: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/4269#issuecomment-7207545858 (first push), https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/4269#issuecomment-7209988799 (merge-time refresh)

## Decisions

`docs/decisions/4269-kernel-plan-converter.md`:
- one rapid plane, the clearance height
- a plunge-feed move down to the approach
- a lift to the clearance height with the `links.rs` note text
- arcs for exact circles only
- chords for leads and helices
- the refusal of a plane that is not the setup XY plane
- "one plan for each level": the caller plans each level and reads the stock state of that level through its `cleared` area; the converter does not re-plan
- the `k3_load` path and its re-pinned row
- the merge of #4254: the rows of #4275, and the K4 crossings pinned as measured (follow-up #4300)

## Not exercised

- No app call and no posted G-code: no recipe calls the converter yet (#3752).
- A plan with an exit in the middle of a level, a pre-drilled or cleared-column entry, and a plan with a lead-in were not built from the stages. The unit tests cover air entries, stay links, lifts, exits and arcs.
- `UNKNOWN_STEP`: no other step kind exists, so no test can make one.
- No heavy step (P2).

Effort: max
